details:
For about two weeks, SteamVR crashes with Error -203 every time I join an instance with more than 5–6 players while their avatars are loading. It happens in every instance with a lot of people in it, I tried in instaces with 12, 19, 25 and 40+ people, not just specific worlds or users. Before this I could stay in very crowded instances with all avatars shown (including heavy ones) without any problems, on the same hardware.

Key observations:

Desktop mode works perfectly. The same crowded instances with all avatars shown give no crash and not even lag. The problem only happens in VR.

With avatars hidden (only friends + a few manually shown), there’s no crash and no lag in VR either.

It’s not VRAM or load. I monitored with Task Manager up to the crash: dedicated VRAM peaks at ~13.8/16 GB, shared GPU memory stays at 1.3 GB, GPU usage is 17–30%, and the GPU is at ~50 °C.

It happens with both Meta Quest Link and Virtual Desktop, so it isn’t specific to the streaming method.

No GPU driver crash. Windows Event Viewer shows no driver errors (no amdkmdag / Event ID 4101).

What the logs show:

vrcompositor.txt: repeated AcquireSync FAILED with WAIT_TIMEOUT / ReleaseSync FAILED, then Failed Watchdog timeout in thread Render ... Aborting → Error -203.

output_log: VRChat is loading remote avatars (44-player instance) and the log stops abruptly with no exception. The log also shows Unity Version: 6000.0.67f1-DWR and Texture Direct Copy is enabled ... (renderer: Direct3D11).

The timing matches the Unity 6 rollout, and the problem appears only in VR while avatar textures are loading. My guess is that something in the new texture loading path, possibly Texture Direct Copy, stalls the GPU sync with the SteamVR compositor on AMD RDNA4. Is there a way to disable Texture Direct Copy to test this?

What I’ve already tried (no change):

Clean GPU driver reinstall (DDU). Older drivers won’t let SteamVR start.

Reset SteamVR settings; render resolution set to 100% (global and per-app).

Disabled hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling.

AMD Adrenalin at default tuning (no OC/UV); HYPR-RX, Anti-Lag, Chill, Boost, RSR, AFMF and FSR all off; reset shader cache.

Cleared VRChat cache.

Closed Medal, OVR Toolkit and OVR Advanced Settings.

Switched from Quest Link to Virtual Desktop.

System:

GPU: AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT, driver 32.0.32015.12012

CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D

RAM: 64 GB

OS: Windows 11 (build 26100)

Headset: Meta Quest 3 (Quest Link / Virtual Desktop)

SteamVR 2.18.4

VRChat on Unity 6000.0.67f1

Update: if I keep avatars hidden and enable them one by one, I can load every avatar in the instance with no crash and no lag. The crash only happens when many avatars load at the same time (e.g. on joining an instance), not because of the total number loaded.
title: [PC VR] SteamVR Error -203 (compositor watchdog timeout) when avatars load in instances with 5+ players, AMD RX 9070 XT, since Unity 6
